cards.name: Merge
cards.summary: Adds the selected paths into the selected Live Paint group (or combines several selected Live Paint groups into one). The added paths become new edges that split the group into new faces the Live Paint Bucket can fill.
use_for: adding extra divider lines to a Live Paint illustration so new regions can be colored
combining separately built Live Paint groups into one coloring group
avoid: selecting only the Live Paint group: Merge needs the group and the extra paths (or groups) selected together
art that must end up as separate editable shapes: Live Paint faces are not real objects until Object > Live Paint > Expand; for plain split shapes use Pathfinder Divide or the Shape Builder tool

use_for: getting the original line work back out of a Live Paint drawing to redraw or recolor it another way
undoing a Live Paint conversion
avoid: keeping the colors: Release discards every fill and stroke color; use Object > Live Paint > Expand to get filled shapes that look the same

protecting overlying text and graphics while tweaking a shape beneath them

cards.name: Other Layers

use_for: focusing edits on one layer of a busy multi-layer illustration
protecting background, text and guide layers while redrawing one layer

cards.name: Selection
cards.summary: Locks the selected objects: they stay visible and print, but can no longer be selected, moved or edited until they are unlocked (Object > Unlock All).
use_for: pinning a background image or template while drawing on top of it
protecting finished logo parts from accidental nudges
freezing reference shapes used for alignment
avoid: hiding clutter: locked art still shows and prints; use Object > Hide or a template layer
scripts that later need the object: locked items cannot be selected; set pageItem.locked = false first

cards.name: Make Pixel Perfect
cards.summary: Aligns the selected artwork to the pixel grid: straight horizontal and vertical edges are nudged onto whole-pixel boundaries and the objects are marked pixel-aligned, so icons and UI art render crisp on screen instead of with soft antialiased edges.
use_for: icons and UI elements exported as PNG at 1x
screen graphics and web banners with thin strokes
fixing blurry edges on art drawn without pixel snapping
avoid: print artwork: the tiny shifts gain nothing at print resolution and can break exact print dimensions
curved or diagonal edges: they stay antialiased; only straight horizontal and vertical edges benefit

equivalents.CDR: Object/Align and Distribute/Align with Pixel Grid

packaging and merchandise previews for pitches and social posts
checking how a design reads on a curved product before printing
avoid: a flat comp on a plain rectangle (poster, screen): just place the art; Mockup is for curved or angled product surfaces

cards.name: Add Anchor Points
cards.summary: Adds one new anchor point halfway between every pair of neighbouring anchor points on the selected paths, without changing the shape (the harvest audit took a rectangle from 4 to 8 points). Running it again doubles the count again.

cards.name: Average...
cards.summary: Moves the selected anchor points to their average position, so they line up on one horizontal or vertical line, or all stack on one spot.
cards.how: Select two or more anchor points with the Direct Selection or Lasso tool, then pick the Axis: Horizontal (points line up on one horizontal line), Vertical (on one vertical line) or Both (they collapse onto their common centre). Both followed by Object > Path > Join welds two open ends into a single point.
use_for: lining up the end points of lines exactly before joining them
making the top or bottom points of a drawn shape perfectly level
collapsing two open ends into one corner point
avoid: aligning whole objects: use the Align panel; Average moves anchor points, not objects
points selected with the Selection tool: that selects every point of the path, which then collapses the whole shape

cards.name: Clean Up...
cards.summary: Deletes invisible clutter across the whole document: stray points (lone anchor points), unpainted objects (paths with no fill and no stroke) and empty text paths, each chosen by a checkbox.
